_help: Edit text here (or in the studio), then run: node shared/build.mjs instagram (from design/carousels). Markup: *word* = the red error marker, \n = line break.
docTitle: Edge cases: 8 real bugs from things users really type (Instagram)

slides.title: Her surname is Null, and websites say she *left it blank*
slides.sub: This is an edge case, the kind of input we're sure no user will ever type. Here are seven more that really happened.

slides.title: Real users double-click, switch tabs and lose their network halfway
slides.body: They're not doing anything strange. They are just being users.

slides.title: One double click, two orders
slides.body: The fix is to give each order its own key, so the same order sent twice only counts once.

slides.title: $15 of gift cards became *$20*
slides.ledgerLabel: Same transfer, sent twice at once
slides.body: Egor Homakov, a researcher, found this race condition in Starbucks gift cards. The code assumed the two transfers would happen one after the other.

slides.title: 1 left in stock, *2 sold*
slides.body: Two people click buy in the same second. Both see one item left, and now we have sold an item that we do not have.

slides.title: The name O'Brien can break a query
slides.body: The apostrophe is the character that starts and ends text in SQL. If your code glues the name straight into the query, it breaks.

slides.title: His licence plate said NULL
slides.body: Security researcher Joseph Tartaro got the plate in California. Then tickets that were not his started coming to him. He told the story at DEF CON in 2019.

slides.title: 29 February 2012 + 1 year = a date that doesn't exist
slides.body: That's how part of Microsoft's cloud, Azure, went down on leap day in 2012. The code added one to the year.

slides.title: Adébáyọ̀ has 7 letters. Some code counts 13 bytes
slides.body: Letters with accents and tone marks take more than one byte each. So a 10-character limit can turn away a short Yorùbá name.

slides.title: Which edge case have you seen in production?
slides.body: You can't predict every single one. If you wait till you can, you probably wouldn't ship anything.
